quote: Although not in and of themselves a mitigating factor, the impact of intergenerational trauma resulting from Mr. Beynon's Indigenous background is something that the court is able to consider in determining the extent of his moral culpability.
reason: Court considered Gladue and intergenerational trauma for culpability; residential schools only from Gladue report.

quote: I am mindful that the African Nova Scotian and Indigenous communities are over-represented in custody. Racism and systemic discrimination have contributed to this. I should always keep incarceration as a last resort and pay particular attention to this reality in Ms. Robinson's case.
reason: Racism and Indigenous background reduced culpability; three years, below range, despite seriousness.

quote: She grew up in an atmosphere of dislocation, discrimination, and alienation as a result of government policies that subjected her father to the ravages of residential schooling and deprived her mother, father and siblings of their rights as Aboriginals .
reason: Appeal court applied Gladue, cited residential schooling and discrimination, cut sentence to ten months.

quote: his moral culpability is reduced considering his life circumstances as an Indigenous person. These circumstances include ... family displacement (including for residential schooling) ... These are direct reflections of the impact of colonialism and racism on Indigenous communities.

quote: Both of his parents attended residential schools, and it appears that they have suffered the traumatic impact of that, including substance abuse and violence in their own relationship.

quote: In my view, the Gladue report does not lay anything other than the most tenuous foundation to say that that nexus exists in this case.

reason: Judge took Métis heritage into account; appeal court upheld sentence at low end of range.

quote: I do take into account Mr. Sunshine's aboriginal status as well as his disadvantaged background. While that has some impact on the result I reach, given the nature and seriousness of the offence, it is not of great significance.
